podcast.body: Track six on "The Joshua Tree," notable for having never been played live by U2 for a long time. The difficulty in performing it live stemmed from its plodding, half-time groove, which made it challenging to sustain audience attention. Adam Clayton later confirmed that the band redesigned the groove to make it more suitable for live performance, and the brass sections might be performed using synthesizers in a live setting. "I think the groove works on record but it's a hard one to pull off live because it plods along."
